title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 97% implied probability against a US default by 2027 reflects Congress's consistent pattern of raising or suspending the debt ceiling ahead of deadlines, as seen in multiple prior negotiations, combined with the Treasury's use of extraordinary measures to manage cash flow. Bipartisan recognition of severe economic fallout from missed payments on Treasury securities underpins this pricing, reinforced by historical precedent where even divided government has reached last-minute agreements. Primary drivers include ongoing appropriations processes and institutional incentives to preserve full faith and credit. Realistic scenarios that could still shift odds involve prolonged congressional impasse after the next statutory limit, though such outcomes have repeatedly been avoided through procedural votes or omnibus packages.
